newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rhone shares placed at 177.50 Ffr.
newsitem.headline: Rhone shares placed at 177.50 Ffr.

text.p: The shares in French chemicals group Rhone-Poulenc sold by state agency Consortium de Realisation (CDR) were placed at a price of 177.50 francs per share, fund managers said on Thursday.
CDR, the agency grouping the assets to be sold of state bank Credit Lyonnais, said early on Wednesday it sold 14.9 million Rhone-Poulenc shares, or a 4.6 percent stake, to institutional investors.

Fund managers said institutional investors who bought the shares would receive a 1.20 franc premium, a "clawback", in the event that any of Rhone-Poulenc's core shareholders wished to exercise a pre-emptive right to buy the shares. The shareholders have one week to use their rights.
The core share holders are AGF, Societe Generale, BNP, AXA, Fiat and Credit Suisse.
A CDR spokesman said the shareholders were not expected to exercise their rights.
